hero.title: Qadam design system
hero.lead: The tokens, components and patterns every screen of the platform is built from — from the incubator form to the Demo Day projector mode. Light and dark themes, three languages, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility.

colors.title: Colour
colors.lead: The palette of the university’s site (mooc.kaztbu.edu.kz): a teal accent, navy for headings and dark panels, green-grey surfaces; statuses, gold and copper come from the same set. Contrast is recalculated for the current theme.
colors.primaryNote: #067A75 = 700 for text and buttons (5.2 : 1); #09BAB2 = 500 and mint #83DCD5 = 300 for accents
colors.goldNote: #B07A00 → #E2B53E. Awards and highlights; text uses step 700
colors.text: Text and contrast on the surface
colors.inkName: Navy and deep teal · ink, deep
colors.inkNote: #102945 for headings and dark buttons; #082834 and #0E3A3F for dark panels

typography.title: Typography
typography.lead: As on the university’s site: Google Sans for the interface and large numbers, Literata for headings. Both fonts are open (OFL), self-hosted and checked by a script against the full Kazakh alphabet.
typography.headline: From idea to market — one step
typography.sample: KazUTB students launch projects that change Kazakhstan
typography.alphabetNote: Glyphs are verified in CI with npm run fonts:check for every font subset.
typography.numbersNote: Equal-width digits in KPIs and tables

shape.title: Shape and depth
shape.lead: A 4 px grid. Buttons, fields and icon buttons are square; cards and panels have a 14 px radius, as on the university’s site. Shadows are soft and wide, only for what floats above the page.
shape.motionNote: 150–250 ms, ease-out for entrances, springs for dragging and toggles.

buttons.title: Buttons
buttons.lead: As on the university’s site: square buttons in spaced capitals. One main button per screen, the rest quieter; teal turns navy on hover.
buttons.iconButtons: Icon buttons with tooltips and shortcuts
buttons.onDark: On a dark panel, and the section kicker

steps.problem: The problem and who has it

q1.question: Will the AI mentor write the project for me?
q1.answer: No. In coach mode the mentor asks questions and suggests methods; in co-author mode it proposes wording that you decide whether to apply.

q2.question: Who can see my project?
q2.answer: You choose: the team only, the whole university or the public showcase. Unit economics and technology can be hidden separately.

q3.question: Can I work from my phone?
q3.answer: Yes. All incubator steps, the mentor chat and competition applications are designed for smartphones.

first.title: Test your pricing hypothesis
first.text: Ask 10 farmers: would they pay 4,500 ₸ a month for an irrigation forecast?

second.title: Find an agritech mentor
second.text: Yerlan Seitzhanov holds office hours on Thursdays — 2 slots are free.

workspace.stageLocked: The stage unlocks once the previous one is completed.
workspace.mentor1: You described farmers as one group. How do 5-hectare and 500-hectare farms differ — in budget and in who makes the purchasing decision?
workspace.student1: Small farms decide for themselves; large ones have an agronomist and a buyer. Their budgets differ too.
workspace.mentor2: Good observation — these are two segments with different buying paths. I suggest recording them separately:
workspace.suggestionText: Segment A: family farms of 5–50 ha, the owner decides. Segment B: agricultural holdings above 500 ha, the agronomist and buyer decide.
workspace.applied: The wording was added to the “Segments” field
workspace.ask: Ask the mentor about this step…
workspace.stepLead: Describe exactly who faces the problem: segments, their size and one or two personas with real pains.
workspace.checklistTitle: What to strengthen to complete the step
workspace.checklist1: Estimate the size of each segment (bottom-up, with a source)
workspace.checklist2: Confirm the persona's pains with at least three interviews
workspace.segmentsHint: 2–3 segments with traits that make them findable
workspace.segmentsValue: Farms in the Turkistan and Zhambyl regions growing cotton and melons on irrigated land.
workspace.painsValue: Irrigates “by eye” following the neighbours' schedule; in summer the canal runs short, and over-watering salts the soil and cuts the yield.
